features: A working round timer in the first screen: three-minute rounds, a minute's rest, twelve rounds, with the digits turning red for the last ten seconds
The week's timetable straight underneath, worked out from the visitor's clock: what's on now, the next bell, and what has already finished
First-session booking that starts with four photo tiles (never boxed, done a bit, competed, it's for my kid), then a day this week, then two fields
Real gym photography, membership with a monthly or annual switch, and a book and call bar that stays on screen on phones
name: Southpaw
short: A boxing club site run by a live round timer, with the week straight under it.
long: Ring black, chalk white and one corner red. The first screen is a real ringside photo and a working round timer (start, pause, reset, twelve three-minute rounds with a minute's rest), with this week's timetable straight underneath and tonight's next bell worked out from the visitor's own clock. Booking a free first session starts with four photo tiles, so a beginner and a parent each see themselves before they pick a day.
proves: Somebody who has never boxed can pick a level, pick a night this week and be booked in about twenty seconds.
story: Gyms sell on atmosphere and then hide the timetable three clicks deep. This one puts the noise and the booking in the same place, so the page feels like the gym and still books the session.
